item.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO; CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO and Harvey Jones first board chair
item.description: Nvidia's 8-K says the board accepted Jensen Huang's resignation as president, CEO and director on 11 November 2026, effective immediately, and appointed CFO Colette Kress, 59, interim CEO while it searches internal and external candidates; she stays CFO. Harvey C. Jones, a director since 1993 and former Synopsys CEO, becomes the company's first board chair. The board says operations, customer commitments and the product roadmap continue without interruption, and fiscal Q3 results stay on 17 November. Nvidia gave no reason; the exit follows the board's 8 November independent review of reports that Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort, and press reports (TechCrunch, CNBC) link it to personal-conduct disclosures. Shares fell about 10% to 12% on 12 November; CoreWeave and Nebius also fell. Caveat: TechCrunch counts about $36 billion of Nvidia cloud-service commitments and large investment and credit-guarantee positions in neoclouds and labs; whether the new leadership keeps that financing posture is unknown. Country conversion: the main US financier of neocloud GPU demand is now under interim management. [Signal 62, Confirmed, via Nvidia 8-K and newsroom, 12 Nov 2026; TechCrunch; CNBC; AP] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Nebius beats on Q3 revenue but trims 2026 guidance as third-party capacity slips into 2027; lifts 2026 capex to about $27 billion
item.description: Nebius reported Q3 2026 revenue of $980.8 million, up 571%, adjusted EBITDA of $465.8 million and quarterly capex of about $7.3 billion. It cut 2026 revenue guidance to $3.0 billion to $3.2 billion (from $3.0 billion to $3.4 billion) because some third-party capacity due this year moved into 2027 (Reuters: first half; the CFO said the second quarter), with the contracts still in place, and said its more than $7 billion ARR target arrives about two months late, in February. 2026 capex rises to about $27 billion from $20 billion to $25 billion. For 2027 it guides revenue of $12 billion to $13 billion, capex of $40 billion to $45 billion for more than 1 GW of new capacity mostly at owned sites, 75% to 85% of that capex funded by customer prepayments ($17 billion to $20 billion) and asset-backed financing, and pre-tax break-even in Q4 2027. Contracted power target of 5 GW by year-end is unchanged. Shares fell about 16%. Caveat: Nebius is Amsterdam-listed in name but much of the capacity cited (New Jersey) is US; the delayed third-party sites are not named. Country conversion: neocloud demand is intact, delivery of colocation capacity is the bottleneck. [Signal 54, Confirmed, via Nebius Q3 2026 results and call, 12 Nov 2026; Reuters; CNBC] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Andhra Pradesh summit: ReNew plans a 1 GW green data centre in Anakapalli; CleanMax and Neysa a 2 GW compute campus in Kurnool
item.description: At the CII Partnership Summit in Visakhapatnam on 12 November 2026, ReNew Energy Global announced about Rs 80,000 crore of Andhra Pradesh investment, including Rs 67,000 crore for a 1 GW green hyperscale data centre in Anakapalli (CNBC-TV18). Separately CleanMax signed an MoU with the AP Economic Development Board for a roughly Rs 50,000 crore clean-power complex (3 GW wind and solar, 1 GW pumped hydro) with its own distribution licence to supply a 2 GW compute factory in Kurnool district with Blackstone-backed Neysa, which anchors 1 GW of IT load; Moneycontrol reports Rs 8,000 crore for the Kurnool project and commissioning targeted by March 2028. Caveat: MoU and summit announcements, not financial close; each element is reported by one outlet here and no GPU supply is named. Country conversion: Andhra Pradesh is stacking gigawatt-class campus pledges on captive renewable power. [Signal 48, Single-source, via Moneycontrol and CNBC-TV18, 12 Nov 2026 (CII Partnership Summit, Visakhapatnam)] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: AWS opens its South America (Chile) Region to select customers, backed by more than $4 billion of investment
item.description: Amazon said on 11 November 2026 that its first Chile region, and third in Latin America, is operational in early access for select customers including BancoEstado, BTG, Cencosud, Itau and Ripley, with general availability expected by the end of 2026. Amazon plans to invest more than $4 billion in Chile and estimates more than $7.5 billion of GDP contribution and about 4,100 jobs a year. The region launches with core compute, storage, networking and database services; Bedrock and SageMaker AI arrive within the first year. DCD reports the Santiago facilities are air-cooled with no ongoing cooling-water draw. Caveat: no MW figure and no GPU or Trainium capacity disclosed at launch. Country conversion: Chile gets in-country hyperscale capacity, AI services to follow. [Signal 46, Confirmed, via Amazon, 11 Nov 2026; DCD, 12 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Kraft Group floats a 900 MW, $16 billion data centre campus in Sutton, Massachusetts
item.description: A memo from Sutton town manager Austin Cyganiewicz to the Select Board says the Kraft Group, with Unified Global Packaging Group, is planning a data centre campus at Unified's Parkway property: two buildings of about 250,000 sq ft and roughly 90 MW each from 2029, then two more a year to 2033, drawing about 900 MW at full build-out and more than $16 billion of private investment by the developer's estimate. Talks with the regional grid operator for power are under way and reclaimed water would be used for cooling. The memo projects about $10.4 million a year in property tax by 2031, rising to $27.8 million, against a projected 2027 town levy of $32 million; a town meeting vote is targeted for May 2027. Caveat: the proposal is tentative, no application has been filed, and residents raised noise and moratorium concerns; under a state executive order, projects over 25 MW need local approval and a community benefits agreement. Country conversion: a large New England campus attempt in a state that now requires local sign-off. [Signal 44, Single-source, via Sutton, MA town manager memo via DCD, 11 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: BloombergNEF counts 181 GW of on-site gas generation proposed for data centres in the US, UK and Europe because of grid delays
item.description: A BloombergNEF report published 11 November 2026, as reported by The Guardian, finds data centres planned across the US, the UK and mainland Europe propose on-site gas plants totalling 181 GW, with about 90% of on-site gas planned in the US, where full rollout would emit about 345 million tonnes of CO2e a year. BNEF projects AI data centre electricity demand near 2,354 TWh by 2035, about 7% of global demand, and warns that 'temporary' bridge generation risks long-term lock-in. The Guardian notes UK sites such as Wapseys Wood and Quest Park are seeking on-site gas while awaiting grid connections. Caveat: proposed capacity, not built or permitted; figures are as reported by The Guardian, not read from the BNEF report itself. Country conversion: behind-the-meter gas is becoming the default US route around interconnection queues. [Signal 46, Single-source, via BloombergNEF via The Guardian, 11 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: SoftBank books a $3.7 billion loss after changing procurement plans for US AI data centre power equipment
item.description: SoftBank Group reported a fiscal Q2 net loss of 1.12 trillion yen (about $7 billion) on 10 November 2026, including a 597.2 billion yen (about $3.7 billion) loss from changes to procurement plans for power-generation equipment for its US AI data centre projects; reports break it into about $2.85 billion of non-refundable advance payments and $0.88 billion of contract modifications and settlements. Cumulative payments for such equipment, for projects like the PORTS-Pike campus in Ohio, reached $9.48 billion at end-September. SoftBank said it had pre-bought gear fearing shortages and long lead times, and reiterated a 20-year, 8 GW lease with OpenAI in Ohio. Caveat: SoftBank did not say which equipment or vendors were affected or whether site timelines change. Country conversion: a leading US power-first campus sponsor is writing off pre-bought generation, a sign of plan churn behind headline gigawatts. [Signal 47, Confirmed, via SoftBank Group FY2026 Q2 results, 10 Nov 2026; CNBC; Reuters; Bisnow] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Boise passes an immediate six-month moratorium on data centres of 100,000 sq ft or 20 MW and up
item.description: The Boise City Council voted unanimously on 10 November 2026 for an emergency ordinance, proposed by Mayor Lauren McLean, that stops the city accepting or processing applications for data centres of 100,000 sq ft or more or using 20 MW of power, effective immediately, while it reviews code and studies water, energy, noise and safety impacts. The mayor said no large applications are pending. Oklahoma City extended its own moratorium the same night (KOKH). Caveat: pre-emptive; it does not touch Meta's operating Kuna site or proposals outside city limits such as Rhea Data south of Boise. Country conversion: local pauses keep spreading after voters backed limits in 40 of 41 November ballot measures. [Signal 38, Confirmed, via Idaho Capital Sun, City of Boise, KTVB, 10 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Anthropic's amended IPO filing says its $34.9 billion August compute deal with Lambda is now terminable after Lambda missed a facility-lease deadline
item.description: Anthropic's second S-1 amendment, filed 10 November 2026, says that under its August 2026 agreement with Lambda, about $34.9 billion of a roughly $41.3 billion set of Lambda commitments running into 2034, either party may terminate if Lambda did not secure the facility lease by a specific date; Lambda did not, so the agreement is currently terminable by either side. Neither party had given notice and Anthropic says it does not currently intend to terminate. The same filing raises Anthropic's Microsoft commitment to at least $47.2 billion and up to $49.2 billion between November 2026 and June 2033, against $44.9 billion in the 2 November filing. Caveat: the filing does not name the facility; press reports from September tied the roughly $35 billion deal to a Hut 8 campus under development in Nueces County, Texas, which is not confirmed here. Country conversion: the largest single US neocloud contract now hinges on one site lease. [Signal 60, Confirmed, via Anthropic S-1/A (Amendment No. 2), SEC, 10 Nov 2026; The Information; DCD, 11 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: CoreWeave Q3 revenue $3.66 billion, backlog $132.5 billion, still guiding 1.85 GW active power by end-2026
item.description: CoreWeave reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $3.66 billion, up 168% year on year, and a net loss of $709 million, and raised 2026 guidance to $13 billion to $13.3 billion of revenue and $1.275 billion to $1.375 billion of adjusted operating income. Revenue backlog rose to about $132.5 billion at 30 September from $104.2 billion at 30 June. Management still expects 1.85 GW of active power by the end of 2026 and $37 billion to $39 billion of 2026 capex, said almost all its power is online or permitted and under construction, and said it does not plan parent-level unsecured debt through 2027 at current yields, relying on customer prepayments, vendor financing and asset-level secured debt. CEO Michael Intrator said a sector-wide construction slowdown could keep GPU pricing higher for longer. Caveat: debt was almost $47 billion at quarter end and some CoreWeave bonds recently yielded above 16% (CNBC). Country conversion: US neocloud capacity is backlog-rich but financing-gated. [Signal 52, Confirmed, via CoreWeave Q3 2026 results and call, 10 Nov 2026; CNBC; Reuters] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Integra-linked filing proposes an $8 billion, up to 756 MW data centre in Quanah, Texas
item.description: 19000-200 Holdings, LLC, whose address matches turnkey builder Integra, filed with the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation for a 288,355 sq ft single-story data centre at 4628 Four Corners Road, Quanah, Hardeman County, with construction from November 2026 to the end of December 2028 and $8 billion of investment, per DCD. Integra's project website puts the campus at up to 756 MW with closed-loop cooling. The site is under 30 miles from Childress, where IREN and Crusoe are developing campuses. Caveat: end user undisclosed; the filing comes as Texas governor-elect Hinojosa has pledged to halt new data centre approvals pending new rules. Country conversion: the North Texas Panhandle corridor keeps drawing gigawatt-class filings into a tightening state regime. [Signal 40, Single-source, via TDLR filing and Integra project site via DCD, 10 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: The Information reports at least $7.5 billion of Nvidia hardware reached Chinese companies since 2023 through a network linked to a Megaspeed executive
item.description: The Information reported on 10 November 2026, citing two people familiar, that at least $7.5 billion of Nvidia hardware has been shipped to Chinese companies since 2023 through a network linked to Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Nvidia customer Megaspeed whom US officials reportedly concluded was a Chinese intelligence asset (New York Times, 29 October). Nvidia's board has opened an independent investigation, President Trump said the FBI is looking into it, and a shareholder class action was filed in San Jose; Nvidia shares fell a further 4% to 6% on 10 November after a roughly 4% drop on 9 November. Caveat: single-source figure, not confirmed by Nvidia or US authorities, and the export-control status of the shipments is not established. Country conversion: if borne out, a multi-billion-dollar leak of US accelerators into China via Singapore, inviting tighter end-use checks. [Signal 48, Single-source, via The Information via Yahoo Finance, 10 Nov 2026; CNBC, 10 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Saudi National Infrastructure Fund signs up to SAR 2.5 billion of GPU and grid financing for HUMAIN
item.description: Infra and HUMAIN signed two facilities on 8 November 2026, announced 9 November: up to SAR 1.1 billion (about $293 million) for GPU procurement equal to about 25 MW of IT load, and up to SAR 1.4 billion (about $373 million) for substations, transmission and grid connections sized for up to 1 GW of future IT capacity. They are the first deals under Infra's AI Data Center Financing Program and convert part of a non-binding SAR 4.5 billion framework announced at Davos in January 2026. Caveat: the 1 GW is grid readiness, not committed compute; GPU vendor not named. Country conversion: Saudi Arabia is using state development finance to pre-build grid for AI campuses. [Signal 45, Confirmed, via Saudi Press Agency and HUMAIN, 9 Nov 2026; Arab News] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Norway halts new grid reservations for data centres until as late as 1 August 2027 and plans a licensing regime
item.description: Norway's transmission operator Statnett on 9 November 2026 paused new grid capacity reservations for data centres and the processing of new facility-functionality approvals, including applications already received for plants on the 420 kV grid, until new technical requirements are approved by the regulator RME, expected no later than 1 August 2027. The same day the government said it will introduce a licensing (concession) regime for existing and future data centres, favouring those serving defence, emergency services, health and other critical functions, and said crypto mining will not count as socially useful. Statnett figures: about 800 MW connected, 4.2 GW reserved, 9.1 GW in the queue and a further 18 GW requested, against national peak demand of just over 25 GW. Caveat: connected and already-approved facilities are unaffected, and Statnett may still process some smaller plants due before August 2027. Country conversion: one of Europe's cheapest-power hosts closes its queue to new large AI loads for up to nine months. [Signal 58, Confirmed, via Norwegian Government and Statnett releases, 9 Nov 2026; DCD; DLA Piper; Enerdata] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: SpaceX files for a roughly $24 billion gas-fired power plant and super-compute facility at Starbase, Texas
item.description: Reuters reported on 9 November 2026, citing a public hearing notice, that SpaceX plans a gas-fired power plant and super-compute facility in Starbase, Texas with an estimated $24 billion of capital investment for its initial phases, and has applied for a property tax abatement and an economic development agreement that the Starbase City Commission will consider on 9 December. SpaceX would build, own and operate the facilities; an affiliate has filed for an 8-mile gas pipeline to Starbase due in service by January 2027. Caveat: the notice gives no generating capacity or compute scale, and the abatement size and term are undisclosed; this sits alongside the separate Cochise County, Arizona filing heard the same day. Country conversion: a second behind-the-meter frontier campus filing in Texas despite the extended state pause. [Signal 44, Single-source, via Reuters, 9 Nov 2026 (Starbase public hearing notice)] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: SoftBank, Grab and PETROS sign joint development agreements with $1.85 billion seed capital for Malaysian AI infrastructure targeting 5 GW
item.description: SoftBank Group and Grab announced on 9 November 2026 joint development agreements, with Sarawak's state oil company PETROS, for $1.85 billion of initial combined seed capital to build AI infrastructure in Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia, with a long-term target of 5 GW or more. The Sarawak project is $1 billion ($800 million SoftBank, $100 million Grab, $100 million PETROS), building on an 8 October Kuching framework agreement; the Peninsular project is $850 million ($650 million Grab, $200 million SoftBank), led by Grab. SoftBank agreed in principle to a five-year lock-up on Grab shares it holds directly. Caveat: capital is staged against development and customer-contract milestones; JV formation and investment terms remain subject to definitive agreements, and no hyperscaler customer, site size or power contract is named yet. Country conversion: a second gigawatt-scale Malaysian programme in a week after Google's $15 billion commitment. [Signal 52, Confirmed, via SoftBank Group and Grab joint release, 9 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Israel's National AI Directorate sets a 300,000-GPU, 2 GW sovereign AI target and a domestic frontier model
item.description: Erez Askal, head of the National AI Directorate in Israel's Prime Minister's Office, presented the national AI strategy at Tel Aviv University's AI & Cyber Week on 9 November 2026 (Ctech): a sovereign AI stack with about 300,000 GPUs (100,000 for academia, government, defence and startups; 200,000 for technology companies and data centres), about 2 GW of electricity capacity for AI infrastructure, data centres and semiconductor manufacturing, and an Israeli frontier model built with partner countries. Caveat: these are targets from a conference presentation; no budget, timeline, sites or vendors were given, and Ctech notes Israel's grid is already strained by data centre demand. Country conversion: Israel states a quantified sovereign compute goal for the first time. [Signal 34, Single-source, via Ctech (Calcalist), 9 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Anthropic buys about $3.4 billion of commitments for 1.7 GW of gas-fired generators from OnePWR, FT reports
item.description: The Financial Times reported on 8 November 2026, and CNBC carried, that Anthropic bought commitments for 1.7 GW of heavy-duty gas-fired generators from San Antonio-based OnePWR Solutions in late September for about $3.4 billion, including the engineering and construction capability to install them. Anthropic did not acquire OnePWR and no staff moved; secondary coverage says the deal took over OnePWR's existing Caterpillar orders. Caveat: FT is the only primary source and cites one person familiar; Anthropic has not confirmed, and sites for the generators are not disclosed. Country conversion: a frontier lab is buying its own US behind-the-meter generation queue position, roughly $2 million per MW, alongside its Riot and TeraWulf leases. [Signal 46, Single-source, via Financial Times via CNBC, 8 Nov 2026; DCD, 9 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: PPL's Invitium agrees terms to build about 2 GW of generation for QTS in Salem Township, Pennsylvania; advanced-stage pipeline reaches 35.3 GW
item.description: On its Q3 2026 call (6 November) PPL said Invitium Energy, its 51% joint venture with Blackstone Infrastructure, agreed all key commercial terms under a letter of intent with QTS for about 2 GW of generation for QTS's Salem Township, Luzerne County data centre: two combined-cycle gas plants plus fuel cells and battery storage, a 20-year initial term with five-year renewals, and an estimated $5 billion to $7 billion of project investment at $2,500 to $3,500 per kW. Fuel cells and batteries could be online from 2029 and the gas plants in 2032 and 2033. PPL's advanced-stage Pennsylvania data centre pipeline rose for an 11th straight quarter to 35.3 GW (up 3.5 GW), with about 11.4 GW under signed service agreements and 8.5 GW under construction (up 2 GW); 300 MW is energised so far. Caveat: the QTS terms are non-binding pending a long-form agreement, and PPL's plan excludes Invitium. Country conversion: a US utility building dedicated generation for a single campus rather than waiting on PJM. [Signal 50, Confirmed, via PPL Q3 2026 earnings call, 6 Nov 2026; DCD, 10 Nov 2026; Lehigh Valley Business] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Equinix opens SG6, among the first Singapore data centres built under the post-moratorium call-for-application regime
item.description: Equinix opened SG6, its sixth Singapore IBX, on 6 November 2026 with an initial investment of about $290 million, 8 MW and about 1,550 cabinets in phase one and up to 20 MW at full build-out. Equinix says SG6 is among the first data centres developed under Singapore's Data Centre Call for Application framework, designed for liquid-cooled GPU deployments at a target PUE of 1.20; a co-innovation facility with NUS follows in 2027. Singapore's Senior Minister of State Tan Kiat How gave the launch keynote. Caveat: capacity is small next to Johor and Batam campuses across the border. Country conversion: Singapore's controlled-allocation regime is now delivering live AI-ready capacity. [Signal 30, Confirmed, via Equinix release, 6 Nov 2026; MDDI keynote; DCD, 10 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: SpaceXAI applies for a 747-acre, up to 6 GW data centre campus in Cochise County, Arizona; zoning decision 9 December
item.description: SpaceXAI, via affiliate Tombstone Resources LLC, has applied to Cochise County, Arizona for a special development permit for up to nine 493,000 sq ft data centre buildings on 747 acres near the Willcox Playa, on land owned by AEPCO and Southline Transmission and adjacent to AEPCO's 626 MW Apache Generating Station (DCD, 6 November 2026). The application describes four 1.5 GW phases, construction from March 2027 if zoning is approved, about $3.6 billion of company-funded power infrastructure ($500 million for Phase I) and a 24 GWh battery system. The county decision is set for 9 December. Caveat: 6 GW is the company's full-build claim; timing depends on grid upgrades, and chips, power and cooling to fill it are not secured. Country conversion: a gigawatt-class US campus filed outside the Texas pause map. [Signal 44, Corroborated, via DCD, 6 Nov 2026 (Cochise County application); Arizona Daily Star; Data Center Feed] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Kazakhstan signs preliminary deals with Gaw Capital, Boosteroid and Firebird for 480 MW more at Ekibastuz Data Center Valley
item.description: Kazakhstan's prime minister's office said on 6 November 2026 that Gaw Capital, Boosteroid and Firebird signed preliminary agreements adding a combined 480 MW at Data Center Valley in Ekibastuz (second phase), with talks on a further 240 MW with China Energy, Aleria and Energy Capital Global; no per-company split was given (Southward Tech, 9 November). The government targets 1 GW by 2029. Phase one is three centres totalling 304 MW: a 68 MW site targeted for Q2 2027, Firebird's 164 MW site with excavation 70% complete, and a 72 MW centre in Q4. Firebird said in October it holds a US export licence for 45,000 Grace Blackwell GPUs. Caveat: the new deals are preliminary and come via a government statement. Country conversion: Kazakhstan adds phase-two demand from both US and Chinese-linked parties. [Signal 32, Single-source, via Southward Tech, 9 Nov 2026 (Kazakhstan PM office, 6 Nov)] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: TeraWulf locks Fluor EPC and a Google credit backstop for Anthropic's ~401 MW Justified campus in Kentucky
item.description: TeraWulf's 6 November 2026 Q3 release and Fluor's 4 November newsroom say the companies signed a definitive EPC for three data centre buildings at the Justified Data Campus in Hawesville, Kentucky, with early works already underway and Fluor to recognize the award in Q4 once pricing for the first two buildings is finalized. TeraWulf states a 20-year Anthropic lease for about 401 MW of critical IT capacity (~$19 billion contracted revenue over the initial term), a Google credit backstop for anticipated project financing supporting that lease, and phased ready-for-service from late 2027 through Q2 2028. Separately TeraWulf lifted Muskie contracted power from 500 MW to 1,000 MW subject to Kentucky PSC approval. Caveat: site development capex ex-compute is cited in investor materials around $4.0–4.5 billion in secondary summaries; stick to the IR/Fluor figures above for Wire. Country conversion: Anthropic offtake plus investment-grade-linked financing and named EPC move a Kentucky GW-class campus into construction. [Signal 57, Confirmed, via TeraWulf IR, 6 Nov 2026; Fluor newsroom, 4 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: EuroHPC voids all AI gigafactory tenders for technical reasons; large sites due 3 December, medium sites pushed to 4 February
item.description: The EuroHPC Joint Undertaking updated its AI Gigafactory call (EUROHPC-2026-CEI-AIGF-01) on 5 November 2026: for undisclosed technical reasons all draft and submitted tenders in the system will not be considered and must be recreated under new submission links. The deadline for Lot 1 is extended to 4 February 2027 to give member states time to complete required steps, while Lot 2 stays at 3 December 2026, both 17:00 Luxembourg time. DCD (10 November) describes the programme as four smaller sites eligible for up to EUR 100 million each in Phase I and three larger sites up to EUR 200 million each. Caveat: DCD's report reverses which lot moved; this item follows the EuroHPC call page. Country conversion: Europe's sovereign compute procurement slips again, and no site awards are possible before 2027. [Signal 46, Confirmed, via EuroHPC JU call page (updated 5 Nov 2026); DCD, 10 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: About 600,000 Nvidia H200s sit in Hong Kong as Beijing withholds large-scale import approval, Reuters reports
item.description: Reuters reported exclusively on 5 November 2026, citing two people familiar, that about 600,000 Nvidia H200 chips are stored in Hong Kong awaiting shipment to mainland China because Beijing has not approved large-volume imports. Several major Chinese internet companies have each received about 10,000 H200s in recent months and small quantities have moved via intermediaries. One person said an eight-card H200 server was offered for more than 6 million yuan (about $900,000) in mainland China by end-October, about three times a year earlier, and Blackwell servers for more than 20 million yuan. Caveat: Reuters is the only source; MIIT, NDRC, Nvidia and the Chinese buyers did not comment. Country conversion stall: US-licensed supply exists but China's own approvals are the binding constraint. [Signal 42, Single-source, via Reuters via Investing.com, 5 Nov 2026; DCD, 6 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Texas governor-elect commits to keep the data centre moratorium until new laws pass; analysts put about half the US hyperscale pipeline at risk
item.description: Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa said she will extend outgoing governor Greg Abbott's pause on new data centres, which she called a scam, until the legislature enacts her Texans First Data Center Priorities: local votes on projects, no NDAs, proof households will not pay more for power or water, no subsidies, union labour, and water contracts voidable if they threaten community supply (DCD, 5 Nov). BMI estimates 53% of hyperscaler pipeline growth sits in newly flipped governor states (Texas, Georgia, Ohio, plus Pennsylvania, where Josh Shapiro was re-elected) and says the Texas pause could plausibly run into late 2027; Cleanview counts 159 GW, or 41% of planned US data centres, in states whose new governors back a pause. Caveat: Hinojosa takes office in January 2027, ERCOT expects its large-load review to end in December, and BMI calls a national moratorium low-probability; the pipeline figures are analyst estimates, not cancellations. Country conversion: Texas, the largest US growth market, is now set to stay paused past the audit. [Signal 64, Corroborated, via DCD, 5 Nov 2026 (Hinojosa; BMI and Cleanview report); Hinojosa campaign release] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: US voters back data centre restrictions in 40 of 41 local ballot measures; OpenAI answers with a Compute Campus Policy
item.description: Of 41 local ballot measures across 10 states on 3 November, voters backed restrictions or rejected pro-development measures in all but one, per Ballotpedia and CNBC (Axios counts 43-1 with about 75% average support). On 5 November OpenAI published a Compute Campus Policy and National Community Compact: for data centres it owns and operates it will seek community input, publish construction plans, stop using NDAs with public officials and pay the full cost of its power, and it urged lawmakers to write similar rules into law. Reuters reported the Philadelphia semiconductor index fell 8% on 5 November and CoreWeave and Nebius dropped 11% and 15%; UBS estimated about 30% of expected 2028 US capacity additions could be at risk. Caveat: OpenAI's commitments cover only sites it owns and operates, not leased capacity; ballot counts differ slightly by tally. Country conversion: US siting now carries explicit community and ratepayer conditions. [Signal 58, Corroborated, via CNBC, 5 Nov 2026; Axios, 5 Nov 2026; DCD; Reuters via Investing.com] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Microsoft declines an option to more than double its Texas compute contract with Nscale
item.description: The Financial Times reported on 5 November 2026, and Reuters confirmed via a person familiar, that Microsoft will not exercise an option to more than double its existing agreement with Nscale in Texas, a potential extension worth tens of billions of dollars. Per DCD, Microsoft already operates about 230 MW at Nscale's leased Ionic Digital site in Barstow; the declined option, which Nscale says was closer to 500 MW, was for behind-the-meter capacity at Nscale's own adjacent Ward County site. The source says the decision was made months ago, before Nscale's September IPO filing, and does not change its disclosed $103 billion backlog, about 40% of it Microsoft; Nscale has since signed Figure for 100,000 Vera Rubin GPUs at the site and is talking to other customers including hyperscalers. Caveat: FT is the primary source; Microsoft and Nscale did not comment. Country conversion: a hyperscaler passes on gigawatt-scale Texas neocloud capacity weeks after exiting Nscale's Essex site. [Signal 48, Corroborated, via FT via Reuters (Investing.com), 5 Nov 2026; DCD, 5 Nov 2026; AFR] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Princeton Digital Group secures about $1.3 billion of green financing for its 200 MW JH1 campus in Johor
item.description: Princeton Digital Group announced this week about $1.3 billion (about RM5.1 billion) of green financing, underwritten by Affin Bank, HSBC, Maybank, OCBC, Standard Chartered and UOB, to continue building its JH1 campus at Sedenak Tech Park, Johor. JH1 is designed for 200 MW of high-density AI and cloud load; its first 52 MW phase was completed in July 2025 and a third building topped out in late 2025. Caveat: no tenant or new MW timing was disclosed. Country conversion: Johor capacity keeps converting into bank-financed build, a day after Google added $15 billion for Malaysia. [Signal 40, Confirmed, via DCD, 5 Nov 2026 (PDG announcement)] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: IndiaAI's next 10,000-GPU compute round halves the entry bar to 512 units; bids close 13 November
item.description: C-DAC's request for empanelment (RFE C-DAC/GPU/01/2026, issued 7 October) for the IndiaAI Mission seeks up to 10,000 GPUs, TPUs and other accelerators, with bidders needing 512 units at a single Indian data centre, half the 1,000-unit bar of the first round. After two corrigenda, bids close 13 November and technical bids open 14 November. Providers serve five years with data, control planes and backups kept in India, must have at least INR 120 crore average turnover, and can qualify with a purchase order backed by a INR 10 crore guarantee. The existing IndiaAI portal lists 45,081 units, led by 16,496 H100, with lowest bids of INR 153 per H100-hour on demand. Caveat: single trade-press report of a government document; Stage 1 sets no prices, and new capacity may not go live until late 2027. Country conversion: India widens its sovereign compute pool to smaller domestic operators. [Signal 36, Single-source, via Communications Today, 5 Nov 2026 (C-DAC RFE)] More: https://compute.world/wire
